POSITION.canonical_name: The Twin at the Year Gate

Social.headline: Your friends are equals, or they are not friends.
Social.recognition: You keep a few equals close and everyone else at a friendly distance. Because you seem to need nothing, you attract people as capable as you are, and the ones who want support look elsewhere. Your circle is small and sturdy, and you feel its gaps more than you admit.
Social.lived: The friends you made as a child were your equals, children who kept pace with you and stood up for you in turn. By your teens you had kept only the level friendships, letting the rest go without a fuss.

Family.headline: You are the relative who never needs rescuing.
Family.recognition: You do your part in the family before anyone thinks to ask, and you expect nothing back. Because your first home rewarded self-reliance, you call your relatives when there is something to offer, rarely when there is something to ask. Your relatives hear from you less than they want, though you mean the quiet as a kindness.
Family.lived: An older relative in your first home made a point of standing on their own, and you copied it before you understood it. You asked for less with each year you grew, and the adults around you praised you for it.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Twin inside the Year Gate

Family.headline: You meet your family as an equal.
Family.recognition: You stand level with your relatives, present and practical and never fussy. Because closeness in your first years came from standing side by side, you show tenderness late and mostly through what you do. You turn up to fix a family problem before anyone asks, saying little about what you feel.
Family.lived: In your first home you grew up beside another child who stood level with you, and the two of you handled most things together. Long before fifteen you settled your own quarrels, and the adults were the last to hear of them.

Growth.headline: You grow from trusting yourself first.
Growth.recognition: Every skill you have began with deciding that you could do it. Because you learned early to depend on yourself, nobody can push you into learning, and you take instruction only from someone you have chosen. You pick things up fastest with one equal working beside you, a peer you have let that close.
Growth.lived: From your first years you taught yourself what the adults around you had not shown you, and you kept quiet about how hard it was. You came into your teens with a stubborn way of learning, on your own terms and at your own pace.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Twin at the Month Gate

Career.headline: You do your best work as nobody's junior.
Career.recognition: You work as a peer of whoever runs the project, whatever your level, and you expect to be judged on what you finish. Because your own effort is how you measure yourself, you slow down the moment a manager hovers and speed up once you are left alone. What you want from a job is a standard you set and meet yourself.
Career.lived: Since your late teens you have been the one handed the job nobody else would finish alone. Your moves between teams and roles have come each time someone else took the credit for your work.
Career.lived_past: From sixteen to your mid-thirties you were the one handed the job nobody else would finish alone. Your moves between teams and roles came each time someone else took the credit for your work.

Social.headline: Your friends are your equals, or they drift.

Social.lived_past: Through your Rising Chapter your closest friends were people at your own stage, classmates and colleagues who grew up beside you like siblings. Among them you learned to settle your own trouble first and to mention it once it was solved.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Twin inside the Month Gate

Your output rises with every piece of real freedom you get, and a manager who checks in daily costs you more than a lower salary would.

Growth.headline: Your skills are yours, and nobody can take them.

Because you trust only what you have built yourself, you keep going alone long after a second pair of eyes would have helped. Your progress is fastest the moment an equal works beside you, and that is the moment you keep putting off.

Social.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties your closest friendships were between equals, people who never needed you to rescue them. You kept every friendship level, with nothing owed in either direction.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Twin at the Hour Gate

POSITION.canonical_name: The Rival at the Year Gate

Family.lived: You have become the relative who hosts since your late forties, the one whose table the people after you head for first. You see your own habits of ease in how they now treat their guests, down to the second helping.
Family.ahead: From your late forties you become the place the people after you come to rest, the slow meal and the spare bed and the evening nobody rushes. You enjoy them more as they grow easy around you, unhurried and well fed.

Career.headline: Your work runs on appetite, not ambition.
Career.recognition: You work best on things that feed people in some way, a meal or a garden or a well-made thing. Because making something well gives you more pleasure than climbing, you turn down promotions that would take you away from the work itself. You do more in a happy month than in a pressured year.
Career.lived: Since your late forties your work has turned toward making, hosting and finishing the projects you had put off for years. You have made some of your best things in this stretch, better received than anything from your busier decades.
Career.ahead: Your working life slows to the pace that suits you from your late forties, and the work you make for others becomes the work you enjoy most. You are paid for it in thanks as well as money, a trade that pleases you more each year.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Artisan inside the Hour Gate

Family.headline: Your later family is the people at your table.
Family.recognition: You treat anyone who eats at your home every week as family, and a regular guest matters to you as much as a cousin. Because cooking for people is the pleasure you never tire of, you keep inviting them in years when others have given up hosting. You would feel lost in a home that no one visits, and yours stays busy because of it.
Family.lived: Your home has filled with the people after you since your late forties, and with friends who come for the food. You have hosted more in this stretch than in any earlier decade, and lately the people you once fed have started cooking for you.
Family.ahead: Your table fills up from your late forties, and the people after you stay longer each year for rest as much as for food. You feed them without fuss, and the comfort of your kitchen becomes the thing they miss most when they are away.

Health.headline: Your body grows easier to live in each decade.
Health.recognition: You keep your body well through good meals, gentle movement and people nearby, and it answers in kind. Since rest comes easily to you, a good week of it stretches into a slow month before you notice. You do best on pleasure rather than effort, and a forced regime wears you out faster than an idle week.
Health.lived: Your sleep has deepened since your late forties and your appetite has steadied, and you have enjoyed your food more than ever. Your energy has dipped in the stretches when you were on your own too much, and it has come back each time the house filled up again.
Health.ahead: From your late forties your body settles into an easy rhythm, with long meals, unhurried walks and sleep that comes without effort. You stay strong while there are people to eat with, and those years suit you better than your busier ones did.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Virtuoso at the Year Gate

Social.headline: People quote you after one meeting.
Social.recognition: You get noticed in any group, for a quick remark or an opinion nobody else would voice. Because being seen as bright has been part of you since childhood, you feel flat in company that only wants small talk. You keep the friends who enjoy your sharpness for years and lose interest in the ones who only tolerate it.
Social.lived: When you were a child, your remarks were the ones other people repeated, at home and in class. By your teens you had a few friends who loved your wit and one or two adults who had given up on correcting you.

Mind.headline: Your mind gets there first and gets bored first.
Mind.recognition: You spot the weak step in an argument at once, and you say so before the speaker has finished. Since your thinking was praised early for speed, you are careless with the slower parts of a problem. Your mind does its best work on hard problems with someone watching, and it drifts when it has neither.
Mind.lived: You finished the work early at school and went looking for something harder, or for trouble when nothing harder came. By your teens you were teaching yourself subjects well beyond your class and hiding how bored you were.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Virtuoso inside the Year Gate

Family.headline: Your family gets your honesty along with your love.
Family.recognition: You love your family most easily where you are allowed to disagree, and a home that asks you to keep quiet feels cold to you. Because honesty was your first way of belonging at home, you say what others leave unsaid, and a relative or two finds you hard work. Your warmth is real, and it shows most with the people who argue back.
Family.lived: As a child you questioned the house rules that everyone else accepted, and you said so out loud. You reached your teens with a name for being difficult and a sharp sense of which opinions to keep to yourself.

Growth.headline: You grow by doubting what you are given.
Growth.recognition: You improve anything you are handed by questioning it first, a method or a belief or a piece of advice. Since accepting things whole has never felt honest to you, you learn more slowly from instruction and faster from your own mistakes. Your doubt sharpens into skill when it has real work, and it turns on you when it has none.
Growth.lived: You had outgrown some of what your family believed by your teens, and you got there by arguing with it. In school you did best in the subjects that let you question the answer, coasting through the ones that did not.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Virtuoso at the Month Gate

Career.headline: You are hired for your talent and tested on your discipline.
Career.recognition: You do your strongest work where you can be seen doing it, pitching or performing or leading from the front. Because you need honest credit to stay interested, a desk job under close supervision drains you within months. Your sharpest ideas win the meeting, and how far they carry you depends on what you finish.
Career.lived: Bosses have either backed you fully or tried to slow you down since your late teens, and few have stayed neutral about you. You have done your best work for the ones who believed in you, and you have outstayed most of the ones who did not.
Career.lived_past: From sixteen to your mid-thirties bosses either backed you fully or tried to slow you down, and few stayed neutral about you. You did your best work for the ones who believed in you and outstayed most of the ones who did not.

Social.headline: Friends and colleagues either love you or resist you.
Social.recognition: You say the sharp thing in company, the joke that lands too close or the question nobody wanted asked. Because being remembered matters more to you than being liked, you accept that a few people cool on you after a dinner. You are closest to the people who came for that edge and defend it when you are absent.
Social.lived: Since your late teens your friendships have been sorted by what you said in public, in class and at work. You have ended up trusting the people who argued back far more than anyone who simply agreed.
Social.lived_past: Through your Rising Chapter your friendships were sorted by what you said in public, in class and at work. You ended up trusting the people who argued back far more than anyone who simply agreed.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Virtuoso inside the Month Gate

Career.headline: You are paid to make things better.
Career.recognition: You are best in jobs where improving things is the work itself, editing or design or reform of some kind. Because a weak plan is plain to you before anyone asks, you correct work that was never yours to correct. Your value at work grows with every process you improve, and you are known as the colleague who will not let poor work pass.
Career.lived: In class, in teams and in your first jobs you have been the one who said out loud what could be better. You have clashed with bosses over it, and they have been the ones who sent for you when something needed fixing.
Career.lived_past: Through your Rising Chapter, in class and in teams and in your first jobs, you were the one who said out loud what could be better. You clashed with bosses over it, and they were the ones who sent for you when something needed fixing.

Mind.headline: Your mind never stops improving what it sees.
Mind.recognition: You think in revisions, turning over a plan or an idea or your own opinion until it is better, and nothing feels quite finished to you. Since a fault you have noticed stays with you until it is mended, your mind keeps working when the day is over. You sleep best in the weeks when one hard problem has all of your attention.
Mind.lived: Your mind has gone looking for faults since your late teens, in what you were taught and in what you believed yourself. You have changed big views only after arguing yourself into the new one, which leaves you with beliefs that survived your own questions.
Mind.lived_past: From sixteen to your mid-thirties your mind went looking for faults, in what you were taught and in what you believed yourself. You changed big views only after arguing yourself into the new one, which left you with beliefs that had survived your own questions.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Virtuoso inside the Day Gate

Love.headline: You love the person who can answer you back.
Love.recognition: You show love by talking and teasing, and a quiet partner leaves you lonely even in a happy home. Since you feel close only when your mind is met, you pick arguments for the thrill of the reply, and some evenings end colder than either of you meant. You want praise and honesty in the same person and rarely settle for half.
Love.lived: The partners you have chosen so far were quick ones who argued well and laughed at the right moments, and each cold spell between you began with honesty that arrived before warmth. You have come out of them knowing which of your true words a partner can take.
Love.ahead: Love from your mid-thirties fills with talk, and you look for a partner who matches you word for word. In these years you grow closer through what the two of you argue about, and you learn which of your sharpest words to keep for everyone else.
Love.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties your partners were quick ones who argued well and laughed at the right moments, and each cold spell between you began with honesty that arrived before warmth. You came out of them knowing which of your true words a partner could take.

Mind.headline: Your mind is sharpest in conversation with someone close.
Mind.recognition: You think best out loud, with one person close enough to hear the rough version and sharp enough to push back. Because your ideas only feel real once they have been tested on someone, an evening of silence at home leaves you restless. You give a partner your best ideas first and your harshest opinions with them.
Mind.lived: Your best thinking so far has been done in argument, in late talks at home where every point you made was questioned. You have changed your mind only for a partner who argued better, and those talks have given you the sharpest voice in any group.
Mind.ahead: Your thinking grows bolder from your mid-thirties, and the arguments you have at home turn into work you show in public. You become known in these years for ideas first tried on a partner, and you say them more kindly than you once did.
Mind.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties your best thinking was done in argument, in late talks at home where every point you made was questioned. You changed your mind only for a partner who argued better, and those talks gave you the sharpest voice in any group.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Virtuoso at the Hour Gate

Career.headline: Your work says what others will not.
Career.recognition: You do your best work where you can say what you think, and a job that asks for quiet manners tires you. Because your skill has grown faster than your patience for rules, you are better at the job than many who manage it. You judge yourself by the work alone, never by the rank of whoever praised it.
Career.lived: Your work has grown bolder since your late forties, and you have said in public what you once kept back. You have outlasted the jobs that wanted a quieter voice, doing better work in each one that replaced them.
Career.ahead: From your late forties your influence grows as rank starts to matter less, and people begin to repeat what you say. You hear your own voice in the way the people after you argue with you, sharp lines and all.

Growth.headline: You grow by breaking the rule you were given.
Growth.recognition: You grow where someone has said a thing cannot be done, a rule to question or a method to beat. Because being told how bores you before it tires you, you leave a settled position sooner than others think wise. You speak more plainly after every break, whatever it costs you.
Growth.lived: Since your late forties you have said out loud what others kept quiet about, and changed your way of working because of it. You grew more from each break than in the calmer years before, though each one looked risky to everyone watching.
Growth.ahead: Past your late forties the people who once called you difficult start calling you wise, and your arguments get a hearing they never had. You keep your edge in these years by finding one settled idea after another to question.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Virtuoso inside the Hour Gate

Family.headline: Your family stays sharp with talk and argument.
Family.recognition: You love your family through talk, about ideas and plans and whatever they are getting wrong. Because saying the true thing is how you stay close, you are sharper with the people you love than with anyone else, and the gentler ones keep their distance. You want a family with plenty to say, and a quiet week with them is the one you like least.
Family.lived: Since your late forties the talk in your family has got sharper and funnier, and the people after you have learned to answer you back. You have been proudest when one of them beat you in an argument, though you have rarely said so.
Family.ahead: From your late forties the people after you seek you out for talk they cannot get anywhere else. You become the one in your family who says what others will not, with more warmth than you once had.

Mind.headline: Your mind stays quick and restless with every decade.
Mind.recognition: You keep your mind busy with projects and opinions, and an empty week wears you down faster than a hard one. Since an idea feels finished to you only once it has been argued, you go looking for a debate when none comes to you. Your thinking stays quick while it has something to take apart, and it dulls within days when it has none.
Mind.lived: Since your late forties your mind has kept finding new work, a project or a cause picked up whenever an old one ran out. You have argued more with every year, and the arguing has kept your mind younger than your age.
Mind.ahead: From your late forties your thinking turns bolder, and you question ideas you once took on trust. You lose sleep over an idea that grips you until you have said it out loud.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Horizon at the Year Gate

Wealth.headline: For you, money is for moving toward the next opening.
Wealth.recognition: You spend on people and plans easily, and a good opening excites you more than money sitting still. Because the best things in your childhood arrived unplanned, you take bets that frighten more careful people. You find it hardest to keep a store apart from your generosity, and a windfall rarely stays long enough to start one.
Wealth.lived: Growing up you saw money come into your first home through side doors and leave again on visitors and new plans. By your teens you had a quick eye for a chance, and saving was something you had to teach yourself.

Family.headline: Generosity runs in your family, price and all.
Family.recognition: You give freely in your family, the treat paid for and the loan made without terms. Because giving is how you feel close to people, you find it hard to refuse anyone near you. You widen the circle you give to past what you can afford, resenting it only later.
Family.lived: An older relative in your first home kept an open door and spent widely on whoever came through it. Growing up you learned both the warmth of that generosity and what it cost the household.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Horizon inside the Year Gate

Family.headline: Your family holds together across distance.
Family.recognition: You keep close ties with relatives who live far away, and you are the one who calls first. Because distance was ordinary when you were growing up, a long absence never feels to you like a break in love. You are the link between relatives who would otherwise lose touch.
Family.lived: Through your first years your family lived far apart, and visits and calls did the work of living close. You grew up able to go months without seeing a relative and come back as close as before.

Wealth.headline: Your chances with money grow the further you go.
Wealth.recognition: You find your best chances away from home, in a new city or an unfamiliar market or among people you have just met. Because familiar places feel small to you, you look outward for money before you look nearby. You earn far from home and feel safe only once the money is back in one place.
Wealth.lived: When you were young the family's money came from moving, from work taken far off and trade that travelled. You looked past your own streets for every chance to earn, and a coin from a distance pleased you more than any from next door.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Horizon at the Month Gate

Career.headline: You are paid for spotting the chance others miss.
Career.recognition: You do your best work wherever there is something to find, a client or a deal or a gap in the market. Because the search keeps you sharp, a fixed salary and a quiet desk wear you down faster than hard work. You are the colleague people come to first when they need a way in.
Career.lived: Your best career moves since your late teens have come through timing, a job heard about early or an offer made in a casual conversation. Your working life has turned with each better chance, and it has grown wider than any single ladder.
Career.lived_past: From sixteen to your mid-thirties your best career moves came through timing, a job heard about early or an offer made in a casual conversation. Your working life turned with each better chance, and it grew wider than any single ladder.

Wealth.headline: Your money arrives in windfalls and goes to the next chance.
Wealth.recognition: You earn best from timing, a bonus or a sale or a deal that comes good all at once. Because you trust another opening to come, each gain goes straight into the next venture or the next move. Your money moves as fast as your eye for the next deal, and a quiet season finds you rich in plans.
Wealth.lived: Good years and thin ones have followed each other since your late teens, with money arriving in lumps. You have put each windfall into a move or a venture before setting any of it aside, and those ventures have widened your range more than your balance.
Wealth.lived_past: From your late teens to your mid-thirties good years and thin ones followed each other, with money arriving in lumps. You put each windfall into a move or a venture before setting any of it aside, and those ventures widened your range more than your balance.

Social.headline: You know someone for every need.
Social.recognition: You collect contacts the way other people collect friends, and you love introducing people who will get on. Because your network brings you work and money, the useful friendships and the warm ones get mixed together. You give a real friend the same quick hour you give a contact, and the difference is the last thing you notice.
Social.lived: Many of your friendships since your late teens began far from home, over a deal or a trip or a shared plan. You have kept a friend in each of the worlds you passed through, and a few of them have become close for life.
Social.lived_past: From sixteen to your mid-thirties many of your friendships began far from home, over a deal or a trip or a shared plan. You kept a friend in each of the worlds you passed through, and a few of them became close for life.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Horizon inside the Month Gate

Career.headline: You build a career by spotting openings first.
Career.recognition: You are drawn to work where timing matters, buying and selling or finding things before others notice them. Because you read change early, a job where nothing moves bores you, and you leave it sooner than you planned. In any role you end up as the person who sees what is coming next.
Career.lived: Since your late teens your best jobs have been the ones where you could spot a trend early, in trading or sales or finding the right people. With every move you have widened your range of contacts, until a chance reaches you before anyone announces it.
Career.lived_past: In your twenties and early thirties your best jobs were the ones where you could spot a trend early, in trading or sales or finding the right people. With every move you widened your range of contacts, until chances reached you before anyone announced them.

Wealth.headline: Your money comes in strong seasons and quiet ones.
Wealth.recognition: You earn in bursts, a run of good months and a quiet stretch after. Because each good season makes you sure of the next, you spend the winnings on a new chance before you have kept any. You are richer in the middle of each good stretch than after it.
Wealth.lived: What you have earned since your late teens has followed your instinct, with good runs and lean months in turn. By now you know how your own streaks run, a lesson paid for with the gains of good years spent chasing better ones.
Wealth.lived_past: What you earned from sixteen to your mid-thirties followed your instinct, with good runs and lean months in turn. You came out of those years knowing how your own streaks ran, a lesson paid for with the gains of good years spent chasing better ones.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Horizon inside the Day Gate

Love.headline: You fall for people who widen your life.
Love.recognition: In love you fall for the one with plans and friends and somewhere to be. Because range is what draws you, you lose interest within months in a partner who only offers closeness. What you want is someone who brings the world home, and anyone who shuts it out leaves you restless.
Love.lived: The people you have fallen for so far each came with a world attached, a circle of friends or a plan to move or a family that took you in. With each of them, you have stayed a little longer for the life around them than for the person.
Love.ahead: From your mid-thirties love and money start to move together. You choose a partner in these years who brings an opening into your life, and the bond holds for as long as the two of you keep heading somewhere new.
Love.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties the partners you chose each came with a world attached, a circle of friends or a plan to move or a family that took you in. With each of them, you stayed a little longer for the life around them than for the person.

Social.headline: Your friends come with plans.
Social.recognition: You collect friends who are going somewhere, the ones with a trip planned and a contact for everything. Because range is what draws you, you lose touch with friends whose lives stay small, and you feel guilty about it only later. You know a great many people, and you let only a few of them close.
Social.lived: Most of your friendships so far have begun as an invitation into someone else's circle, on a trip or after a move to a new place. You have kept some of those circles longer than you kept the people who brought you in.
Social.ahead: Your circle widens from your mid-thirties through a partner's world, through their friends and their family and their work. In your forties you know more people through a partner's side than through your own.
Social.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties most of your friendships began as an invitation into someone else's circle, on a trip or after a move to a new place. You kept some of those circles longer than you kept the people who brought you in.

Wealth.headline: Your money comes through the people close to you.
Wealth.recognition: You find money through other people, in a tip from a friend or a side venture with someone close. Because your openings arrive through people you trust, you say yes before you read the terms, and you earn in bursts more than in a steady line. The money you make fastest is the money you hold on to least.
Wealth.lived: Your best money moments so far came through someone else, a tip or a job offer or a deal brought to you by a friend. You lost money the same way, on ventures you joined on trust, yet the net of people who bring you chances has only widened.
Wealth.ahead: From your mid-thirties your income starts to rise through the life you share with a partner, through a joint venture, a move or an opening from their side. You will earn more in these years than in all the years before, and you see the part with no clear owner slip away.
Wealth.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties your best money came through someone else, a tip or a job offer or a deal a friend brought you. You lost money the same way, on ventures you joined on trust, yet the net of people who brought you chances only widened.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Horizon at the Hour Gate

Wealth.headline: Your money comes in through side doors.
Wealth.recognition: You notice a chance to earn where others see an ending, a venture someone else gave up on or a deal nobody followed up. Because new money excites you more than kept money, you move it on to the next opening and write down too little of it. You carry your plans in your head far longer than you put them on paper.
Wealth.lived: In the years since your late forties money has reached you through doors you had stopped watching, late ventures and deals brought by people a generation younger. You have built a wide spread of small ventures in place of one steady income, each one opened on a hunch.
Wealth.ahead: From your late forties chances to earn keep arriving from far outside your usual circle, through new projects and through the people after you. You say yes to more of them than anyone your age, happiest when the offer comes from furthest away.

Growth.headline: Every fresh start widens your world.
Growth.recognition: You widen your range whenever life allows, a new field or a new place or a crowd you know nothing about. Because being a beginner keeps you awake and curious, a life that only repeats itself bores you within months. You surprise the people around you with how many times you begin again.
Growth.lived: Since your late forties you have kept moving, into new work, new places and friendships with people much younger. You have come out of each move more curious than people your age, and less settled than anyone expected.
Growth.ahead: Your world gets wider from your late forties, through travel and through work in places that are new to you. You become the one in your family with the newest stories, and the most open to the next change.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Horizon inside the Hour Gate

Family.headline: Your family spreads wide and gathers in bursts.
Family.recognition: You love it best when your whole family gathers for a few full days, and you plan those days months early. Because distance has never felt like loss to you, long gaps between visits pass without worry. You travel far for a short visit, and the people you miss get many arrivals and few long stays.
Family.lived: Your family has spread to new places since your late forties, the people after you settling far from you and from each other. You have travelled more for them than for any holiday, and their streets have grown nearly as familiar to you as your own.
Family.ahead: From your late forties the people after you open new places to you, a spare bed in a far city and a reason to stay a month. Your visits become the link between them, and those gatherings matter more to you than anything you could buy them.

Wealth.headline: Your later money keeps moving, and so do you.
Wealth.recognition: You keep money in motion, in a late venture, a trip or a deal that came through a side door. Because an untouched account feels wasted to you, you put money into movement before you think of reserves. Your money is always on its way somewhere, and it comes back to you by routes nobody planned.
Wealth.lived: Since your late forties your money has come in sideways, through late ventures and deals struck while travelling. You have spent much of it as fast as it arrived, and that motion has kept new chances reaching you.
Wealth.ahead: From your late forties a windfall or an offer from far away reaches you, and a move sets your money going again. You keep most of it in motion from then on, sleeping best while one part stays untouched.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Steward at the Year Gate

Wealth.headline: You know the value of money, and always have.
Wealth.recognition: You spend with a list and save before anyone asks you to, and money that sits unplanned makes you uneasy. Because order around money felt like safety from your first years, you lose more sleep over a careless purchase than it ever cost you. You are slower to enjoy what you have than to keep it.
Wealth.lived: Money at home was counted and spent with care, and you learned what things cost before most children do. By your teens you were already saving what your friends spent.

Family.headline: A careful, orderly home is your idea of love.
Family.recognition: You show love in your family by keeping things in order, the bills paid and the arrangements made. Because care at home looked like provision when you were small, you trust a relative who plans more readily than one who says warm things. You are the one your family calls when something needs organising, and you rarely say no.
Family.lived: Someone in your first home kept the household running on plans and a careful budget, and you watched closely. By your teens you were the child trusted with the money, the keys or the younger ones.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Steward inside the Year Gate

Family.headline: Your family pays back what it is given, and so do you.
Family.recognition: You rely on your family more than on friends, because help between you has come back each time it was needed. Since your first home kept careful accounts, you keep track of what is owed between relatives without saying so. You give help readily, and a debt left open sits on your mind until it is settled.
Family.lived: As a child you knew that money at home was handled carefully and that nothing was spent without a reason. Early on you counted your own money and saved it the way the household did.

Wealth.headline: Your money grows quietly from early habits.
Wealth.recognition: You save without thinking about it, a little from everything, and spending without a reason feels wrong to you. Because careful habits were normal in your first home, you build wealth slowly and steadily, and few people notice until it is large. You enjoy keeping money more than spending it, and a big purchase stays on your mind for weeks.
Wealth.lived: You kept coins and small earnings longer than your friends did as a child, and nobody had to tell you to. You learned early that money kept quietly was money that stayed, a habit you have never lost.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Steward at the Month Gate

Career.headline: You are the one trusted with the books.
Career.recognition: You notice the figure that does not add up before anyone else opens the file, and things run better near your desk. Because steady work is what you offer, you take on extra tasks without asking for a raise. You carry more of the work than your pay shows, and the whole team runs on your numbers.
Career.lived: You have been given responsibility early in every job since your late teens, a budget or a set of keys or a team's accounts. Your promotions have come steadily, each one a little later than your work deserved.
Career.lived_past: From sixteen to your mid-thirties you were given responsibility early in every job, a budget or a set of keys or a team's accounts. Your promotions came steadily, each one a little later than your work deserved.

Wealth.headline: Your money arrives on time and keeps arriving.
Wealth.recognition: You earn a regular income and build on it month by month, with raises won through steady work. Because predictability makes you feel safe, you distrust any money that comes too easily. Your wealth grows in a straight line, the shape you like best.
Wealth.lived: The money you have counted on since your late teens has been the salary, raised a step at a time and planned for well in advance. You have kept to your plan through lean months and good ones, building savings that have grown every year.
Wealth.lived_past: Through your Rising Chapter the money you counted on was the salary, raised a step at a time and planned for well in advance. You kept to your plan through lean months and good ones, building savings that grew every year.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Steward inside the Month Gate

Career.headline: Every step you earn at work, you keep.
Career.recognition: You do your best work in a job you can stay in and get better at, with clear tasks and fair pay. Because you value what you can explain and defend, you distrust shortcuts and the people who take them. Underrated in the early years of any role, you outlast most of the people who underrated you.
Career.lived: Your working life has moved forward one step at a time since your late teens, with each job adding a skill you kept. Your pay has risen with every one of those skills, earned in full and owed to nobody.
Career.lived_past: From sixteen to your mid-thirties your working life moved forward one step at a time, with each job adding a skill you kept. Your pay rose with every one of those skills, earned in full and owed to nobody.

Wealth.headline: Your savings grow quietly, year after year.
Wealth.recognition: You save a part of everything you earn, and a steady rise in your accounts pleases you more than any sudden gain. Because security is what you are working for, you spend only after you have counted what will be left. Your caution keeps you safe, and a good year feels to you like relief more than joy.
Wealth.lived: Even in lean months you have put money aside since your late teens, and your savings have grown more than people expected. You have turned down exciting offers that asked too much risk, and none of those refusals has cost you a night of sleep.
Wealth.lived_past: You put money aside even in the lean months of your twenties and early thirties, and your savings grew more than people expected. You turned down exciting offers that asked too much risk, and none of those refusals cost you a night of sleep.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Steward inside the Day Gate

Love.headline: You love by keeping a life running for two.
Love.recognition: You show love by providing, the rent covered and the car serviced before a partner thinks to ask. Because steady provision is how you feel secure, you trust a partner who treats shared money as carefully as you do. You let romance fade when the accounts fill every evening.
Love.lived: The partners who have lasted with you so far cared about upkeep and careful money as much as you did. You have kept the everyday running so well in each of them that you noticed the quiet in the romance only afterwards.
Love.ahead: From thirty-five on, love becomes the steadiest thing in your life, a partnership built on joint accounts and savings set aside for both of you. Your warmest seasons in these years are the ones where romance keeps its place beside the upkeep.
Love.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties the partners who lasted cared about upkeep and careful money as much as you did. You kept the everyday running so well in each of them that you noticed the quiet in the romance only afterwards.

Family.headline: You keep a household that never runs short.
Family.recognition: You keep your household running, the cupboards full and the bills paid before they are due. Because a well-kept home is how you show love, you feel uneasy when things at home are left undone. Your family feels safe without knowing how much you do, because you rarely tell them.
Family.lived: In every home you have shared, you have been the one who knows where the spare keys and the papers are. Your careful keeping has carried relatives through lean weeks, with something always put by for whoever needed it.
Family.ahead: From your mid-thirties your household runs on what you put by, the savings and the repairs done before anything breaks. You spend these years keeping it stocked and mended, and every lean spell that passes through finds it ready.
Family.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties you were the one in every shared home who knew where the spare keys and the papers were. Your careful keeping carried relatives through lean weeks, with something always put by for whoever needed it.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Steward at the Hour Gate

Wealth.headline: Your money gets steadier every decade.
Wealth.recognition: You plan for the long run even when the present is messy, and a small regular saving pleases you more than a big win. Because security matters more to you than excitement, you judge a year by what you kept rather than what you earned. You are building something slowly, and you know it.
Wealth.lived: Since your late forties your accounts have settled, the debts cleared and the savings finally visible. You became the one in your family with enough, and you have quietly paid for more than you mention.
Wealth.ahead: The slow years of saving start paying you back in your late forties, and money stops being something you check every week. You spend on the people you love without a second look at the budget, because the budget has held for decades.

Family.headline: You end up as the one who provides.
Family.recognition: You show love for the people who rely on you by making sure they are covered. Because provision is how you say what matters, you would rather pay for something than talk about it. You want everyone who comes after you to be safe, and you plan for it years early.
Family.lived: You have covered the gaps in your family since your late forties, paying the fees and the deposits before anyone had to ask. You have earned the family's trust one settled bill at a time.
Family.ahead: From your late forties your family leans on what you have saved, and you give it calmly. You become the relative everyone trusts with arrangements, saying in words at last some of what your money already says.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Steward inside the Hour Gate

Family.headline: Your family rests on what you quietly arrange.
Family.recognition: You keep your family covered, the bills paid and the plans made for whoever needs them. Because care for you means provision, you say almost nothing about what you have arranged. You prefer it when your family sees the calm and not the work behind it.
Family.lived: Since your late forties you have kept a steady store for your family, quietly topped up and ready before anyone asks. You have shown the people after you how to be careful with money mostly by example, and they have spent more wisely for it.
Family.ahead: From your late forties the people after you build their own lives on what you have saved and set aside for them. You are the steady keeper behind them, and they learn only later how much of their footing you paid for.

Health.headline: Your body does best on steady upkeep.
Health.recognition: Your body gets the same care as your accounts, with regular walks, plain food and early nights. Because routine is what keeps you feeling safe, small daily care suits you better than any sudden effort. You catch the first sign of tiredness early and spend your energy as carefully as your money.
Health.lived: Since your late forties your energy has held steady, because you kept your sleep and your habits in good order. You have more of it in reserve than people who spent theirs freely, and that reserve has been worth every early night.
Health.ahead: From your late forties your body repays the care you keep giving it, with steady energy and regular sleep. You outlast people who run themselves down, and every ordinary habit turns out to have been worth its cost.

Wealth.headline: Your money ends up settled and secure.
Wealth.recognition: You keep reserves for every possible need, and a full account calms you more than any purchase. Because security is what you work for, you spend on others easily and on yourself with reluctance. You have more put by than you let yourself spend.
Wealth.lived: Since your late forties your finances have settled, and your household has felt the hard times around it less than most. You built your savings slowly and kept them whole through every lean year, and they have become the fund your household falls back on.
Wealth.ahead: From your late forties your money stays steady while others worry, and your plans for it land where you intend. You find that part of what you saved was always meant for you, and spending it on yourself stops feeling like a loss.

POSITION.canonical_name: The General at the Year Gate

Social.headline: People respect you first and like you second.
Social.recognition: You walk into a group and people sort themselves around you, some squaring up and others stepping aside. Because respect is what you learned to earn first, you are slow to relax with new people, and you test them before you trust them. You keep the few friends who push back when you push.
Social.lived: As a child you were the one others looked to in a fight or a dare, and you did not give way easily. Your friends by your teens were either as tough as you or kept at a distance, and you learned diplomacy slowly.

Career.headline: Authority keeps finding you, and the hard tests with it.
Career.recognition: You end up in charge in most places you work, before you have asked for it. Because hard tests feel familiar to you, you take on serious work that makes others nervous. You rise through the hardest jobs and find easy ones dull within months.
Career.lived: Pressure beyond your age reached you in your first years, a job at home or a team to lead or younger children to mind. The weight felt heavy at the time, but you came out of it tougher than most of your friends.

POSITION.canonical_name: The General inside the Year Gate

Family.headline: You carry more for your family than anyone knows.
Family.recognition: At home you fight your family's battles, and you take on their problems before they ask. Because you learned early to carry weight without help, you find it hard to let anyone see you struggle. You are the strength your family leans on, though you have told few of them what it took to build.
Family.lived: Through your first years at home you carried a weight few people saw, hard stretches and heavy demands and worries beyond your age. By your teens you were the one your family turned to in a hard week, holding firm without being asked.

Growth.headline: Hard years are the ones that grow you.
Growth.recognition: You grow when life is hard, and you lose direction when it gets too easy. Because difficulty was where you first found your strength, you sign up for the harder option by choice, and a year with nothing hard in it leaves you restless. You have done your best learning in stretches other people would call their worst.
Growth.lived: Each hard year of your childhood left you more capable than the one before, at school or at home or in a sport. You came to trust difficulty more than ease, and by your teens you went looking for it.

Health.headline: Your body is strong and holds its strain.
Health.recognition: Your body keeps pushing under strain, long after most people would stop. Because you learned as a child to hide how tired you were, you notice exhaustion late, and it shows in short sleep and a short temper. You recover well once you finally stop, and the stop comes late every time.
Health.lived: In your first years you were hardy, slow to complain and the last to quit a tough game. Your nerve carried you through hard weeks most children never faced, long before you were fifteen.

POSITION.canonical_name: The General at the Month Gate

Career.headline: Pressure is where your career is made.
Career.recognition: You are given the urgent problem, the team in trouble or the deadline that cannot slip. Because you stay steady when others panic, your managers hand you more than your position covers, and the load keeps growing. You are at your calmest when the stakes are highest, and a quiet week makes you restless.
Career.lived: Your reputation at work has grown out of hard moments since your late teens, the emergency handled or the project rescued. Your promotions have come out of the worst weeks, each one earned by the nerve you showed when a project was close to failing.
Career.lived_past: Through your Rising Chapter your reputation at work grew out of hard moments, the emergency handled or the project rescued. Your promotions came out of the worst weeks, each one earned by the nerve you showed when a project was close to failing.

Social.headline: Your friendships are tested before they are trusted.
Social.recognition: You size up new people by how they act when something goes wrong, and you warm to anyone who keeps their nerve. Because you trust only what has been tested, light talk at a party feels like a waste of your evening. Your friendships are few and serious, and loyalty under strain is the one test you set.
Social.lived: Your closest friends since your late teens have been the people you worked hardest beside, in a tough job or a demanding team. You have come out of each hard stretch with an ally who answers your call at any hour.
Social.lived_past: In your Rising Chapter your closest friends were the people you worked hardest beside, in a tough job or a demanding team. You came out of each hard stretch with an ally who answered your call at any hour.

POSITION.canonical_name: The General inside the Month Gate

Career.headline: You do your best work under real pressure.
Career.recognition: You pick the job with the highest stakes and the tightest deadlines, and you are at your sharpest when it is going badly for everyone else. Because pressure is how you prove yourself to yourself, calm work leaves you flat and restless. What you build fastest is respect, and what you lose first is rest.
Career.lived: You have asked for the hard assignment since your late teens, the failing project or the client nobody else could handle. You have come out of each crisis more trusted, until the hardest work reaches you first.
Career.lived_past: From your late teens to your mid-thirties you asked for the hard assignment, the failing project or the client nobody else could handle. You came out of each crisis more trusted, until the hardest work reached you first.

Health.headline: Your body carries the cost of your pace.
Health.recognition: You run on adrenaline through long weeks and notice the tiredness only when the pressure lifts. Because effort is where you feel most like yourself, you push through poor sleep as if it were part of the job. Your energy runs deep, though you spend it faster than you replace it.
Health.lived: Since your late teens your body has kept pace with demands that stopped most people around you. Your hardest seasons have ended with you worn out for weeks, and each one has taught you to stop a little sooner.
Health.lived_past: In your twenties and early thirties your body kept pace with demands that stopped most people around you. Your hardest seasons ended with you worn out for weeks, and each one taught you to stop a little sooner.

POSITION.canonical_name: The General inside the Day Gate

Love.headline: You love hardest when something is at stake.
Love.recognition: You trust a love that has come through something hard, and you feel closest to a partner in the weeks when everything is on the line. Because pressure is how you know a bond is real, you test a partner without meaning to whenever love runs easy. Your kind of partner has the nerve to stand beside you when it counts.
Love.lived: Your relationships so far have been tested hard, by heavy loads and bad stretches carried together, and the strain itself felt like closeness. From them, you have learned to tell a bond that bends under pressure from one that breaks.
Love.ahead: Love asks more of you from your mid-thirties, a shared load and the pressure of carrying it well. You come through these years closer to a partner when the two of you turn your strength to the same hard task.
Love.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties your relationships were tested hard, by heavy loads and bad stretches carried together, and the strain itself felt like closeness. From them, you learned to tell a bond that bent under pressure from one that broke.

Health.headline: Your body grows strong under hard tests.
Health.recognition: You feel best in the weeks your body is pushed hard, by training, by heavy work or by a goal with real stakes. Because you meet pressure by bracing against it, a long strain at home goes into your sleep before you admit it is there. You recover within days once the fight is over.
Health.lived: Your strongest stretches so far have been the hard ones, when home and work both tested you and you held up on nerve and short sleep. You have come out of each test tougher and with a clear sense of how much you can carry.
Health.ahead: From your mid-thirties a partner who pushes as hard as you do keeps you fit, and a house full of fights wears you out. You are at your strongest in these years whenever the two of you pull in the same direction.
Health.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties your strongest stretches were the hard ones, when home and work both tested you and you held up on nerve and short sleep. You came out of each test tougher and with a clear sense of how much you could carry.

POSITION.canonical_name: The General at the Hour Gate

Career.headline: You come alive when the work gets hard.
Career.recognition: You are the one handed the crisis and the deadline nobody else will carry. Because pressure is where you feel useful, you take on the hard jobs other people step away from. What you find hardest is a calendar with nothing urgent in it, which you fill fast.
Career.lived: Since your late forties you have been the one asked to lead when things went wrong, the rescue job or the project already failing. You came out of each one with more nerve than you took in, and with a name as the person to call.
Career.ahead: From your late forties the work people bring you is the hardest they have, the turnaround or the fight that others back away from. You stay in the thick of it longer than most, still called in when others your age have stopped being asked.

Growth.headline: You grow by using your strength with more care.
Growth.recognition: You change by getting better at pressure, using less force to get the same result. Because you have tested yourself so many times, you know your limits well, and you spend your energy where it counts. You lose your temper less than you did, winning more ground by waiting.
Growth.lived: The hard tests have kept coming since your late forties, and you have met them with better timing and a cooler head. You have picked the battles that mattered and let the rest pass, making fewer enemies than in your younger fights.
Growth.ahead: In the years after your late forties the tests you face are tests of nerve more than strength, and you meet them with a calm that surprises people who knew you younger. You trade force for precision with every year, saving your hardest push for the one moment that decides it.

Family.headline: Your family learns to rise to your pressure.
Family.recognition: You protect your family by making them strong, the hard lesson given early and the risk faced together. Because you trust pressure to build people, you push the young ones harder than outsiders and stand closest to them in a crisis. You are at your best with them in a storm, and less sure of yourself on the calm days.
Family.lived: The people after you have brought you their hardest weeks since your late forties, and you have pushed them to face what scared them. You have watched them come through tougher than they expected, each test leaving them less afraid of the next.
Family.ahead: Past your late forties the people after you take on fights of their own, and they borrow the nerve you showed them. You soften with them as they toughen, the one they want beside them when the stakes are real.

POSITION.canonical_name: The General inside the Hour Gate

Health.headline: Your body stays strong by being tested.
Health.recognition: You treat your body as something to test, with an early start and a tough workout most days. Because strength is part of how you see yourself, you ignore tiredness until it slows you down. Your energy is at its best when the week asks something hard of you.
Health.lived: Since your late forties your body has answered every hard test you set it, and your strength has returned with every new round of training. You have pushed past the point of rest in tired weeks out of pride, and felt it for days afterwards.
Health.ahead: From your late forties you keep finding new tests for your body, a longer distance or a harder season of training, and it rises to each one. You stay fitter than most people your age, and the weeks without a challenge are the ones that slow you.

Family.headline: Your family feels your protection first.
Family.recognition: You stand between your family and trouble, and you meet a threat before anyone else has seen it coming. Because a crisis brings out your best nerve, you are calmest in their worst weeks and restless in their easy ones. You hold the line for them in a storm without being asked, and they know it.
Family.lived: The people after you have leaned on your strength in hard moments since your late forties. You took on the worst of each crisis yourself and kept your own worries out of their sight.
Family.ahead: Past your late forties the people after you turn to you first when things go wrong. You stand beside them through the hardest tests of their lives, and they come out braver for having you there.

Growth.headline: Hard tasks you set yourself keep you growing.
Growth.recognition: You grow the way you always have, by taking on something difficult and holding yourself to it. Because an easy stretch makes you uneasy, you start a new practice or project long after others have stopped, and you finish it. You find unplanned days harder than hard work, and the quiet is what tests you most.
Growth.lived: Since your late forties you have taken on new disciplines one after another, a skill or a sport or a hard new trade, and stuck with each longer than people expected. You have come out of each one steadier, with a nerve that holds where it once shook.
Growth.ahead: From your late forties you grow through challenges you choose yourself, and each one asks more of you than the last. Counting rest as part of the work at last, you keep your strength longer than most people do.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Magistrate at the Year Gate

Social.headline: People trust you before they know you.
Social.recognition: New people give you their trust quickly, and you are offered responsibility in a group before you have earned it. Because a good name was part of your upbringing, you behave in public with care, and you dislike being seen at your worst. You guard your standing more closely than anyone asks you to.
Social.lived: Neighbours and the adults at school trusted you as a child, partly because of the name your family carried. By your teens you were the one picked to lead or represent the group, and behaving well had become your role.

Family.headline: You come from a family that keeps its standards.
Family.recognition: You hold your family's name with pride and some strain, and its standards still shape what you allow yourself. Because what the family stood for was visible to others, you feel its expectations most in public. You honour the values you were given and quietly drop the rules that never made sense.
Family.lived: In your first home there were clear rules and an older relative who held everyone to them. By your teens you knew exactly what the family expected of you, and you met most of it while keeping a few doubts to yourself.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Magistrate inside the Year Gate

Family.headline: Your family's rules still live in you.
Family.recognition: The expectations you grew up with stay with you, and you feel uneasy when a family duty goes undone. Because approval at home came through doing things right, you check yourself against what your elders would think. Your bond with your family is strong and dutiful, with a pull you feel wherever you live.
Family.lived: You knew the rules of your first home without being told, and you rarely needed correcting. You came into your teens holding yourself to an older relative's standards as strictly as if they were your own.

Growth.headline: You grow best inside a clear structure.
Growth.recognition: You grow by finishing what you start, the course completed and the level passed and the standard met. Because order is where you first felt secure, you do well wherever the steps are clear and lose heart when they are not. You climb steadily, further in the end than people who started faster.
Growth.lived: Through your first school years you built a record of steady progress, each year finished well and responsibilities taken on early. By fifteen you were the one the adults in charge trusted with a role, measuring your growth by the steps you had completed.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Magistrate at the Month Gate

Career.headline: Your record earns you rank.
Career.recognition: You climb at work through trust and the job done the proper way, whoever is watching. Because order matters to you, you hold to the rules others bend, and senior people notice. You rise steadily and step back from any risk that could put a mark against your name.
Career.lived: Your record has spoken for you at work since your late teens, each role done by the rules and each title kept clean. You have been promoted on schedule and have rarely had to ask for a step up.
Career.lived_past: Through your Rising Chapter your record spoke for you at work, each role done by the rules and each title kept clean. You were promoted on schedule and rarely had to ask for a step up.

Social.headline: Everyone trusts you with the responsible job.
Social.recognition: Your friends and colleagues hand you the keys, the calendar and the emergency. Because people trust you on sight, you get the duty along with the respect, and you rarely refuse it. Your social life runs on reliability, with less time for fun than the people who lean on you.
Social.lived: From your late teens you have been the dependable one in every group, the friend who organised and the colleague who covered. You have given that role weekends and holidays you planned for yourself, and in return it has earned you standing in every circle you belong to.
Social.lived_past: Between sixteen and your mid-thirties you were the dependable one in every group, the friend who organised and the colleague who covered. You gave that role weekends and holidays you had planned for yourself, and in return it earned you standing in every circle you belonged to.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Magistrate inside the Month Gate

Career.headline: Your career grows steadily inside a structure.
Career.recognition: You are at home inside an organisation with fixed rules and a visible ladder, and you climb it by doing every step properly. Because you need to know where you stand, open-ended jobs leave you uneasy, and a clear title settles you. Your reward is lasting rank, and the price is the freedom to move quickly.
Career.lived: In each workplace since your late teens you have learned the rules faster than anyone hired with you, and you have kept your word in every post. Your seniors noticed your reliability early, and you were trusted with more than your age suggested.
Career.lived_past: Through your Rising Chapter you learned the rules of each workplace faster than anyone hired with you, and you kept your word in every post. Your seniors noticed your reliability early, trusting you with more than your age suggested.

Growth.headline: You grow by moving from one structure to the next.
Growth.recognition: You grow inside a framework, a course or a firm or a discipline, until you have learned everything it can teach. Because loyalty runs deep in you, leaving one structure for a bigger one feels like a betrayal, and you wait longer than you need to. Your growth comes in clear stages, and each one starts when you finally move.
Growth.lived: Since your late teens your growth has come through formal steps, a qualification finished or a rank reached or a role handed to you. You have grown most in the years a structure trusted you with more, when it handed you a clear duty and a clear measure.
Growth.lived_past: From sixteen to your mid-thirties your growth came through formal steps, a qualification finished or a rank reached or a role handed to you. You grew most in the years a structure trusted you with more, when it handed you a clear duty and a clear measure.

Social.headline: People rely on you to keep things steady.
Social.recognition: You are the one who keeps a group working, the colleague who remembers what was agreed and the friend who makes the plan happen. Because order calms you, you take on the organising without being asked, and people come to depend on it. Your place in a circle is quiet, though you decide more than anyone gives you credit for.
Social.lived: Your friendships have grown out of work and shared duties since your late teens, the colleagues you trusted and the seniors who trusted you. Friends you had no shared task with drifted away, and you kept the ones bound to you by a duty for years after the job ended.
Social.lived_past: Your friendships in your Rising Chapter grew out of work and shared duties, the colleagues you trusted and the seniors who trusted you. You kept the friends bound to you by a duty for years after the job ended, while the ones with no shared task drifted away.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Magistrate inside the Day Gate

Love.headline: You love with promises, and you keep them.
Love.recognition: You are drawn to partners with clear values, people who keep their word and expect you to keep yours. Because reliability is what love means to you, you trust slowly and commit fully, and you find casual romance empty. You want a partner you can count on for life and give the same in return.
Love.lived: The relationships that mattered to you have been serious from early on, with plans made and promises kept. You have kept your word in them even after the feeling faded, slow to admit when a promise had outlived the love inside it.
Love.ahead: Love settles into something formal and lasting from your mid-thirties, a public commitment and a shared name for what you are. In the small rituals you keep together, you find the warmth that duty alone never gave you.
Love.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties the relationships that mattered to you were serious from the start, with plans made and promises kept. You kept your word in them even after the feeling faded, slow to admit when a promise outlived the love inside it.

Family.headline: Your home runs on kept promises.
Family.recognition: You run your household on clear duties and fair rules, and the people in it know what to expect. Because order is how you protect the people you love, you notice a broken promise at home faster than a kind word. You know your family feels secure with you, and that some of them wish you were less strict.
Family.lived: Your family life has been built on structure, with set routines, shared duties and arrangements that hold. When others forgot, you have been the one who kept the household's promises, and relatives on both sides have come to trust it.
Family.ahead: From your mid-thirties you speak for your household, the one who signs, decides and keeps the family's word. You add more warmth to its order in these years, and you find your own house easier to live in than it used to be.
Family.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties your family life ran on structure, with set routines, shared duties and arrangements that held. When others forgot, you were the one who kept the household's promises, and relatives on both sides came to trust it.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Magistrate at the Hour Gate

Family.headline: Your word holds your family together.
Family.recognition: You take the formal roles in your family, the one who gives the toast, signs as witness and speaks for everyone when it counts. Because a role tells you where you stand, you keep the family's promises even when others have forgotten making them. You hold yourself to your word more strictly than you hold anyone else.
Family.lived: Since your late forties you have carried your family's formal duties, answering for its name and holding it to what it has agreed. You have watched the people after you learn to hold a promise the way you hold yours.
Family.ahead: From your late forties your word becomes the one that settles family questions, and the family's formal jobs pass to you one by one. You carry them as a duty more than an honour, giving the people after you a fixed point to measure their own choices by.

Social.headline: Your reputation keeps rising, decade by decade.
Social.recognition: You are the person people ask to chair the meeting or hold the keys or settle the dispute. Because you take duty seriously, you say yes to roles others avoid, and your circle trusts you more each year. Even with friends you keep a little formality, finding it hard to let anyone see you off duty.
Social.lived: Your name has carried weight in your circle since your late forties, and groups you once simply belonged to have put you in charge. You gained respect that outlasted any title and found yourself consulted on matters well outside your old work.
Social.ahead: Past your late forties your community keeps giving you positions of trust, the committee to chair or the fund to oversee. You are honoured more in these years than in your busiest working ones, lending your name only to causes you would answer for.

Career.headline: You rise at work by being reliable.
Career.recognition: You are drawn to work that keeps an organisation sound, the standards held and the roles clear. Because you respect structure, you would rather run something lasting well than start something new. You are trusted with decisions others will not make, and with the responsibility that follows them.
Career.lived: Your work has shifted toward oversight since your late forties, a senior post or a place on a board or a role answering for the people below you. You were trusted with the running of things you once only served, a responsibility you have carried without a slip.
Career.ahead: In the years after your late forties you move into roles that govern more than they produce, and your judgement becomes your main asset. You earn a respect in these years that lasts longer than any post you hold.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Magistrate inside the Hour Gate

Family.headline: Your family trusts your word completely.
Family.recognition: You serve your family by keeping its word, the promise honoured and the duty done on time. Because a role is how you know your place, you take the formal jobs in the family that others avoid. You hold that word more carefully than your own feelings, and the family builds on it.
Family.lived: Since your late forties the people after you have taken your word as settled, and they have built their plans on the promises you made them. You have kept every one of them, which has given you a standing in the family that no title could.
Family.ahead: From your late forties the people after you take their sense of what is proper from you, and they hold one another to the rules you kept. You see your own standards in how they keep faith with each other, and that is worth more to you than any honour.

Growth.headline: You grow later by refining what you value.
Growth.recognition: You grow by doing familiar things better, holding the same values to a higher standard. Because consistency matters to you, you would rather do a thing properly than try something new, and the change in you shows up as patience. You redo a job nobody else noticed was wrong, for no reason but the standard you hold yourself to.
Growth.lived: Since your late forties your growth has come through commitments you kept, a practice deepened or a standard raised year by year. Your standing has grown with it, and people have started bringing you the work that has to be done right.
Growth.ahead: Past your late forties you keep improving at what you know well, and each year adds polish more than novelty. You grow wiser through repetition and order, and the people after you hold you up as the example of doing things properly.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Alchemist at the Year Gate

Mind.headline: Your mind works at an angle.
Mind.recognition: You come at problems from an unexpected direction, and the strange angle is the one you take. Because your mind took its own path from the start, a private hunch carries more weight with you than the method everyone else was taught. You trust your mind most when nobody else agrees with it.
Mind.lived: As a child you reached the right answer by routes nobody had shown you, working things out alone with a book or a puzzle. By your teens you were known as the clever one or the odd one, and both were true.

Social.headline: You keep your friends few and your inner life private.
Social.recognition: You prefer a handful of people who really know you to a wide circle who only recognise you. Because you open up slowly, the friends you keep have earned it, and they tell you secrets they tell nobody else. You choose friends for how they think, and one shared odd interest outweighs years of small talk.
Social.lived: Other children took a while to warm to you, because you stood at the edge of each group for a long time before you joined it. By your teens you had one or two close friends who understood you, and they were enough for you.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Alchemist inside the Year Gate

Family.headline: You love your family in an unusual way.
Family.recognition: You show love to your family through ideas and help with problems more than through surface warmth. Because the care you got early was quiet and odd, you trust a relative who understands you over one who fusses, and you feel lonely at noisy gatherings. You come home as the quiet one, a part your relatives have long stopped trying to change.
Family.lived: Instead of the usual fuss you got books, questions and long silences from an adult in your first home who lived in their own head. What you took from it was the habit of answering your own odd questions before you thought to ask anyone else.

Mind.headline: Your mind runs on what you find out alone.
Mind.recognition: You learn best alone, from books and odd sources and your own testing, at a pace no class has ever matched. Because nobody handed you a set path, you trust the understanding you dig out yourself, and you forget what you were simply told. You know a great deal that you have never shown anyone.
Mind.lived: Whatever you were given to read when you were small, you read past it into subjects nobody around you shared. By your teens you knew more about a few odd things than most adults did, mentioning it only to the one or two people who asked.

Growth.headline: Your growth takes the odd route, never the set one.
Growth.recognition: You grow fastest through unusual people and unplanned turns, the odd expert or the subject you stumble on. Because the standard routes never fitted how you learn, you find them dull and leave them early. You grow in your own order, and others notice only when it is done.
Growth.lived: The people who taught you most as a child stood outside the usual line, the neighbour or relative with odd interests who took you seriously. You grew in directions your family could not follow, and stopped expecting them to before you were fifteen.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Alchemist at the Month Gate

Career.headline: Your work starts where the standard method fails.
Career.recognition: Colleagues come to you when a problem has stopped making sense, and you find the angle nobody else tried. Because your value lies in unusual knowledge, you choose a narrow speciality over a broad ladder, and you lose interest in work anyone could do. Your reputation travels further than your rank, and it travels slowly.
Career.lived: Work with an odd corner to it has drawn you since your late teens, a niche most people around you ignored. You have watched people easier to explain win the early promotions and then been sent for when their fixes failed.
Career.lived_past: Between sixteen and your mid-thirties, work with an odd corner to it drew you, a niche most people around you ignored. You watched people easier to explain win the early promotions and then got sent for when their fixes failed.

Mind.headline: Your mind is your trade, and it needs quiet.
Mind.recognition: Your mind goes straight to the corner of a subject everyone else skips, the exception or the case that breaks the pattern. Because your best insight comes in private, open offices and constant meetings scatter you within a day. You guard your quiet hours at work more closely than your free time.
Mind.lived: Your thinking has set you apart at work since your late teens, quick to reach an odd answer and slow to explain it. You have handed project after project to a finisher once the puzzle was solved, because the finishing bored you.
Mind.lived_past: Through your Rising Chapter your thinking set you apart at work, quick to reach an odd answer and slow to explain it. You handed project after project to a finisher once the puzzle was solved, because the finishing bored you.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Alchemist inside the Month Gate
