Mind.headline: Your mind runs best on what others find strange.
Mind.recognition: You think best alone, on problems other people have given up on or never noticed. Because you trust only the conclusions you reached alone, you rework a problem long after others have moved on, and you find small talk harder than hard questions. You keep most of what you know to yourself, and it is the thing that matters most.
Mind.lived: From your late teens your mind went its own way, into a subject or a method most people around you did not follow. You have spent more nights with a question than with company, and the result is a corner of knowledge almost nobody else holds.
Mind.lived_past: In your twenties and early thirties your mind went its own way, into a subject or a method most people around you did not follow. You spent more nights with a question than with company, and the reward was a corner of knowledge almost nobody else held.

Growth.headline: You grow late, and mostly in private.
Growth.recognition: You grow in long quiet stretches that look like standing still, and then you change all at once. Because you change on the inside first, the people around you underrate where you are, and you let them. You are further along than anyone watching would guess.
Growth.lived: Since your late teens your growth has looked slow from the outside, years spent studying or testing or changing direction while friends settled. Most of what you can do now, you taught yourself in those years.
Growth.lived_past: Through your Rising Chapter your growth looked slow from the outside, years spent studying or testing or changing direction while friends settled. Most of what you could do by your mid-thirties, you taught yourself in those years.

Career.headline: Your work pays for what only you know.
Career.recognition: You are the specialist people call when the usual answers fail. Because you trust knowledge you have dug out yourself, you are drawn to a narrow field the mainstream ignores, and you would rather be paid for strange work than praised for ordinary work. You earn more from the niche you choose than any ladder would pay you.
Career.lived: Your working life so far has run underground, in jobs that looked quiet while you were building a skill nobody asked for. You have won roles over people with better connections on the strength of something strange you knew.
Career.lived_past: Until your mid-thirties your working life ran underground, in jobs that looked quiet while you built a skill nobody asked for. You won roles over people with better connections on the strength of something strange you knew.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Alchemist inside the Day Gate

Love.headline: You love best with time alone built in.
Love.recognition: You want someone close, and you also want hours each week that belong only to you. Because you work your feelings out in private, you go quiet before a serious talk, and a partner who presses gets less of you. Your love lasts with someone who waits for you to come back.
Love.lived: The people you have loved so far have fallen into two kinds, those who let your private hours be and those who took your silences personally. You have stayed longest with the first kind, the ones who learned that your quiet was thinking and not distance.
Love.ahead: The bond you make from your mid-thirties takes your private hours as part of love and not a gap in it. You grow closer in these years by bringing back what you worked out alone, the odd idea or the half-solved puzzle, and letting a partner in on it.
Love.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties the people you loved fell into two kinds, those who let your private hours be and those who took your silences personally. You stayed longest with the first kind, the ones who learned that your quiet was thinking and not distance.

Mind.headline: You think alone and speak once you are sure.
Mind.recognition: For days you turn a problem over in private before you say a word about it, and you say it only once you have an answer. Because a half-formed thought feels unsafe to you, the people closest to you hear your conclusions without the reasoning. You let a partner further into your thinking than anyone, and even they see only part of it.
Mind.lived: Your clearest thinking so far has happened alone with a subject, late at night or on long walks away from the people you live with. From those hours you have built a command of one unusual field that nobody at home can follow.
Mind.ahead: From your mid-thirties your thinking deepens and turns toward a single subject you have circled for years. You share more of the work in progress with a partner in these years, and the work gets better for it.
Mind.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties your clearest thinking happened alone with a subject, late at night or on long walks away from the people you lived with. From those hours you built a command of one unusual field that nobody at home could follow.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Alchemist at the Hour Gate

Mind.headline: You see further than you can explain.
Mind.recognition: You see the shape of a problem before anyone has finished describing it to you. Because your judgement rests on patterns gathered from odd corners, you can name the answer long before you can show the working, and people find that hard to follow. You rarely explain how you got there, and some people stop asking.
Mind.lived: Your intuitions have hardened into a private method since your late forties, quick, accurate and hard to pass on. You have been right about what everyone else missed so many times that people now bring you the puzzles they cannot crack.
Mind.ahead: From your late forties your mind keeps sharpening, and you return to the obscure subjects you once put aside. You do some of your best thinking in these years, and it reaches further once someone younger helps you put it into words.

Growth.headline: You become more yourself the further you go from the crowd.
Growth.recognition: With each decade you become more of the odd one, and you stop apologising for it. Because the unusual is where you feel most yourself, you drop the roles and habits that were only for show. You buy the out-of-print book and write to the one person still working on the question.
Growth.lived: A subject most people your age would never touch has become yours since your late forties, and the interests you kept for appearances have fallen away. You have grown harder to place and more at ease with it, the strange one by choice now.
Growth.ahead: You grow from your late forties by mastering one rare thing completely. You go further into it than anyone around you, keeping your method in your head long after others ask you to write it down.

Career.headline: Your work begins where the usual answers run out.
Career.recognition: You are at your best as the specialist, called in for the problem with no known method. Because people value what you alone can see, your name opens doors without a post attached, and you prefer it that way. You turn down steady jobs and say yes to strange problems.
Career.lived: Since your late forties more of your work has come by word of mouth, from people who heard you could solve what others could not. You have built a niche out of the problems nobody else would touch, and it has kept you in demand on your own terms.
Career.ahead: The people after you seek out what you know from your late forties, bringing you the puzzles their own training could not solve. You become the one they consult in private, watching your methods carried into work you will never do yourself.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Alchemist inside the Hour Gate

Family.headline: Your family narrows to a few who understand your silences.
Family.recognition: You keep family life quiet and close, with a small number of people who know when to leave you be. Because your private life comes before a full house, you see your relatives less than they would like and love them no less. You sense trouble in one of them long before anyone mentions it, by an intuition they find odd.
Family.lived: Since your late forties your private work has filled more of your afternoons, and you have welcomed only the quietest visits. You have built a family life with more silence in it than most, and the few who share it know you best.
Family.ahead: From your late forties the people after you come to you for what you understand, more than for company. You draw one or two of them close with your unusual method, and they carry it further than you could.

Mind.headline: Your later mind follows questions nobody else asks.
Mind.recognition: You spend your best hours alone with one odd subject at a time, turning it over until it comes clear. Because understanding is the thing you value most, you guard those hours closely and resent the phone call that breaks them. You surprise people with how sharp you are, and with how little of it you show.
Mind.lived: The questions you think about have narrowed since your late forties to the few that matter to you, and your answers have grown more exact. You have settled things that puzzled you for decades, and you have shared less of what you found than people would like.
Mind.ahead: From your late forties private study of your own choosing fills your days, and you take each question as far as it goes. You give the answers to one or two of the people after you and keep the rest for yourself.

Growth.headline: You grow in later life by keeping only what matters.
Growth.recognition: Interests and habits that no longer tell you anything new fall away, and you hold on hard to the few that do. Because you grow by going deeper more than wider, you look as if you are doing less while you understand more. You care less each year about keeping up, and more about getting one obscure thing exactly right.
Growth.lived: Since your late forties the commitments you took on from habit have gone, the groups and roles that once filled your weeks. You have returned every day to the private practices that remain, and they have given you more than anything new.
Growth.ahead: Your growth from your late forties lies in distilling what you already know, until years of odd learning come down to a few clear ideas. You put those ideas into plain words for the people after you, and they are still using them long after you worked them out.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Sage at the Year Gate

Family.headline: You carry the shelter of your first home.
Family.recognition: The steady, patient care you had early is the measure you hold family to, and you notice quickly when it is missing. Because your first home gave you shelter and someone to learn from, you go to a relative for support before you go to a friend. In return you look after your family the way it looked after you.
Family.lived: Your first home ran on gentle care and help with your schooling, given by an older relative who watched over you. By your teens you had their manners and their love of learning, and people outside the family noticed it in you.

Mind.headline: You are a student for life.
Mind.recognition: You approach a new subject expecting to be taught well, and you go looking for the best teacher before you open a book. Because a guide makes learning feel safe to you, you value a qualification for its own sake. You find it harder to learn where nobody is showing you the way.
Mind.lived: As a child you had books at home and adults who answered your questions, and school came easily. By your teens you drew the special interest of teachers and older relatives, and their attention made you work harder.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Sage inside the Year Gate

Family.headline: For you, family means being looked after.
Family.recognition: Family is your shelter, the place you go back to and the people you look after in turn. Because care at home was steady from the start, you trust your relatives easily and find it hard to believe the worst of them. You take it harder than most when a relative lets you down, because you never expected it.
Family.lived: An older relative looked after you closely when you were small, and you came to rely on their calm. You grew up expecting the world to treat you with the same care, and mostly it did.

Growth.headline: Your growth starts from a safe base.
Growth.recognition: You take your biggest steps from a secure position, with people behind you and a home to return to. Because safety came first in your life, you learn faster when you feel held, and you stall when people you do not trust try to hurry you. You put off a change until the support is in place.
Growth.lived: As a child you tried new things when someone you trusted stood close by, and you held back when nobody did. By your teens you were slower than your friends to try things away from home, because home felt so safe.

Health.headline: Your body recovers best when someone looks after you.
Health.recognition: You get your energy back quickly after tiring weeks and bad nights, and faster still when someone close is fussing over you. Because care was what restored you from the start, you let yourself rest properly only when another person insists. Your body does well on trust, rest and good company.
Health.lived: Whenever you were run down as a child, an older relative was there with an early night and a watchful eye. Growing up, you learned that being looked after was part of getting your strength back, and letting others do it came easily.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Sage at the Month Gate

Career.headline: Your career grows under the people who teach you.
Career.recognition: You pick up a new role fastest with someone senior beside you, and within weeks you know what took them years. Because you learn best under someone's wing, you rarely have to sell yourself, and open competition puts you off. You give your best where trust is already in place.
Career.lived: Older people at work have backed you since your late teens, vouched for you or quietly put your name forward. You have collected qualifications and references in those years that still carry weight wherever you apply, and you have needed to push less than most.
Career.lived_past: From sixteen to your mid-thirties older people at work backed you, vouched for you or quietly put your name forward. You collected qualifications and references that carried weight wherever you applied and needed to push less than most.

Mind.headline: Knowledge becomes second nature to you.
Mind.recognition: You learn by steady absorption, and what you study becomes part of how you think without effort. Because the learning feels natural to you, you forget how much of it you have, and others notice before you do. You underrate your own knowledge more than anyone around you does.
Mind.lived: From your late teens you took in courses, books and advice from people who knew more, and kept nearly all of it. Over those years you learned fastest from the ones who trusted you early, and what they taught has become the base you build on.
Mind.lived_past: From sixteen to your mid-thirties you took in courses, books and advice from people who knew more, and kept nearly all of it. You learned fastest from the ones who trusted you early, and what they taught became the base you built on.

Social.headline: Your friends bring you their troubles.
Social.recognition: You are the friend people confide in, the calm one who listens and gives sound advice. Because being trusted feels like a kind of care to you, you rarely say no, and your evenings fill with other people's problems. You know more about your friends' lives than they know about yours.
Social.lived: Since your late teens your closest friendships have grown out of being taken in, an older colleague who taught you or a friend's family who treated you as their own. You have gone to those people first for advice and learned from them how to listen.
Social.lived_past: Through your Rising Chapter your closest friendships grew out of being taken in, an older colleague who taught you or a friend's family who treated you as their own. You went to those people first for advice and learned from them how to listen.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Sage inside the Month Gate

Mind.headline: You learn steadily, and the learning holds.
Mind.recognition: Week by week you add to what you know, studying in a steady and patient way. Because understanding a thing fully is what makes you feel secure, you read the extra chapter and take the extra course, and you speak on a subject only once you are sure of it. You know far more than you claim to.
Mind.lived: Learning has carried you since your late teens, through courses and qualifications and the teachers who took an interest. You have stayed a student in some form ever since, and it has kept you steadier than most people around you.
Mind.lived_past: Learning carried you from sixteen to your mid-thirties, by way of courses and qualifications and the teachers who took an interest. You stayed a student in some form all through those years, which kept you steadier than most people around you.

Career.headline: Your career rises on what you have studied.
Career.recognition: You are trusted at work because you know your subject properly, and people check their facts with you. Because depth matters more to you than visibility, you leave the self-promotion to others, and promotion reaches you later than your knowledge has earned it. Your standing grows slowly and holds when louder careers fall away.
Career.lived: Your progress at work since your late teens has come through what you studied, with each qualification carrying you a step further. You have proved right every mentor who put your name forward before you felt ready.
Career.lived_past: Your progress at work in your twenties and early thirties came through what you studied, with each qualification carrying you a step further. You proved right every mentor who put your name forward before you felt ready.

Growth.headline: Your growth waits on a readiness you already have.
Growth.recognition: Each step you take comes after the training is done and the support is in place. Because shelter feels like the right place to prepare, you stay in safe roles past the point they teach you anything, and you wait for one more sign that you are ready. You are readier than you feel, and have been for a long time.
Growth.lived: From your late teens you have grown in sheltered steps, under teachers and seniors who prepared you well. You have done better than you feared each time you moved, standing on the base they gave you.
Growth.lived_past: In your twenties and early thirties you grew in sheltered steps, under teachers and seniors who prepared you well. You did better than you feared each time you moved, standing on the base they gave you.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Sage inside the Day Gate

Love.headline: You love the person who makes you feel safe.
Love.recognition: You fall for steadiness, the partner who turns up on time and stays calm when you are not. Because being looked after is how you know you are loved, you relax completely with the right person, and you take their care as a given. You are slow to notice how much they carry, and slower to thank them.
Love.lived: The partners who have mattered most to you so far were the ones who looked after you, practically and without fuss. You have handed whole parts of your life to their care, and found afterwards that you had forgotten how to run them yourself.
Love.ahead: From your mid-thirties love turns into care that runs both ways, and you learn to give back the patience you once took for granted. You notice what a partner carries for you and take some of the weight yourself.
Love.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties the partners who mattered most were the ones who looked after you, practically and without fuss. You handed whole parts of your life to their care, and found afterwards that you no longer knew how to run them yourself.

Family.headline: Your home shelters everyone who walks into it.
Family.recognition: You make your household gentle, with voices kept low and nobody left out. Because care is what steadies you, you look after the calm at home before anything else, and some arguments get smoothed over without ever being settled. You end most days having looked after everyone in the house except yourself.
Family.lived: Your home so far has been the calm house in your family, where people come to be looked after when things go wrong elsewhere. You have kept its peace with steady care and with the things you chose not to say.
Family.ahead: From your mid-thirties the shelter you give starts to work both ways, and a partner looks after you as closely as you look after them. You hold the household together in these years, and you speak up more than you used to.
Family.lived_past: In your late thirties and forties your home was the calm house in your family, where people came to be looked after when things went wrong elsewhere. You kept its peace with steady care and with the things you chose not to say.

Health.headline: Being looked after keeps you strong.
Health.recognition: You sleep well and eat well when someone at home takes care of you, and both slip in the weeks you are left to cope alone. Because being cared for is how your body settles, you get over a hard stretch fastest with a partner close by. You are strongest in the seasons you feel most looked after.
Health.lived: Through the hard stretches so far, the person who checked on you and kept the house running did more for your health than any plan you made. You have learned to accept that care without apology and to give it back in kind.
Health.ahead: From your mid-thirties the care at home runs both ways, and looking after a partner steadies you as surely as being looked after. You feel better in your forties than you have in years, held up by the support you give as much as the support you get.
Health.lived_past: Through the hard stretches of your late thirties and forties, the person who checked on you and kept the house running did more for your health than any plan you made. You learned to accept that care without apology and to give it back in kind.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Sage at the Hour Gate

Family.headline: Your family takes shelter with you.
Family.recognition: When your family needs advice or a calm word in a bad week, you are the one they call. Because protecting the young matters to you deeply, you step in early when someone younger is struggling, and you give more than you are asked for. You are respected at family gatherings more than you are relaxed at them.
Family.lived: Your door has stood open to the people after you since your late forties, and they have brought their troubles through it sure of a patient hearing. You have become their home base, the place they return to first when something gives way.
Family.ahead: From your late forties the people after you look to you for guidance, and for cover when things fall apart. You give both with patience in these years, watching what you taught them carry on in their own lives.

Growth.headline: Teaching is how you grow.
Growth.recognition: You grow each time you pass on what you know, through lessons, letters or the patient answer to a question. Because teaching makes you put your knowledge in order, you understand your own life better each time you explain it. You find purpose in being useful to people who are just starting.
Growth.lived: Since your late forties you have found yourself explaining things you once took for granted, and you have learned as much from it as the people you helped. You have grown more patient and surer of what you know, the guide people seek out on purpose.
Growth.ahead: Your knowledge takes a lasting form from your late forties, a course or a set of notes or a body of advice. You take quiet pride in seeing it outlast your own part in it.

Mind.headline: Your thinking stays quick because people keep asking.
Mind.recognition: You keep your mind in use by answering questions, studying widely and staying in touch with people who want your advice. Because being consulted keeps you alert, you are sharpest in the weeks you are busiest with others. You feel slower in a quiet week, but you pick up the phone yourself before it ends.
Mind.lived: Other people's questions have kept your mind active since your late forties, the advice asked for and the problems brought to you. You have read and studied more in these years than since your schooling, and kept most of it.
Mind.ahead: Past your late forties the people after you bring you their questions, and you take care to teach them properly. You are quoted and asked for more than ever, and most yourself when someone leaves understanding more than they came with.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Sage inside the Hour Gate

Family.headline: Your family looks after you, and you let it.
Family.recognition: Younger people look after you more than you expected, with visits and help and small kindnesses. Because being cared for is what lets you rest, you settle into their care and stop running everything yourself. What you want from your family now is company as much as help.
Family.lived: Since your late forties small acts of care have come to you unasked, a lift or a call or a visit from the people after you. You have let them in, and the family has grown closer around you than it was in your busiest years.
Family.ahead: The people after you gather around you from your late forties as a home base, the place they come back to for advice and support. You become the calm centre of a close family, taking their help as easily as they take yours.

Health.headline: Your health in later life rests on gentle rhythm.
Health.recognition: You stay well on walks, early nights and people who check on you, and you sleep badly in a week without them. Because being looked after restores you, you let others carry your pace for longer than it helps, until days with no effort leave you flat and low on energy. You feel best in a week that holds a small challenge.
Health.lived: Since your late forties your sleep has come more easily, and the care of people close to you has set a gentler pace for your days. Leaning on that support through tired weeks, you have come back from each one sooner than you once did.
Health.ahead: From your late forties your body does well on gentle habits and the company of people who look after you. You hold your strength by learning something new each season, and a class or a guided walk does more for you than a hard workout.

Mind.headline: Your mind stays clear through daily habit.
Mind.recognition: You keep your thinking clear with reading, routine and conversation with people who are kind to you. Because your mind learns best in calm, you avoid arguments and noise, and a year with nothing new to study leaves you restless. You think best with one good question in front of you and a patient hour to answer it.
Mind.lived: Since your late forties daily reading and talks with people you trust have kept your thinking calm. Guided by a few good teachers, you have grown steadier in your thinking each year.
Mind.ahead: From your late forties reading fills more of your days, and you remember more of it than you did in your busiest years. You take up study for its own sake, a course or a long book read slowly, with your judgement growing calmer and surer alongside it.
